reasoning_summary:
Construction (line 0001-0013): Heawood graph = Fano incidence graph, plus a clique on the 7 point-vertices. Point-vertices then have degree 9 and line-vertices degree 3, so every automorphism preserves the two sides and is a Fano collineation; Aut = PGL(3,2) = PSL(2,7), order 168. Correct.

Lower bound: n >= 7 is forced since Aut must contain an element of order 7. For 8 <= n <= 13, sigma of order 7 has exactly one 7-orbit A (two orbits would need 14 vertices); tau of order 7 outside <sigma> exists because PSL(2,7) has 8 Sylow 7-subgroups, giving orbit B. Since |A|=|B|=7 and |A u B| <= 13, A n B is nonempty, so <sigma,tau> is transitive on A u B; any v outside A u B is fixed by both, hence uniformly adjacent/non-adjacent to A u B, so Aut(G[A u B]) embeds into Aut(G) by extending with the identity. All correct.

Case 2 (A != B) checked in detail. v in A\B, w in B\A, WLOG (complement preserves Aut, sigma, tau, A, B) vw is an edge. tau fixes v and is transitive on B, so v is adjacent to all of B. sigma fixes w (w not in A), so sigma^k(v) ~ w for every k, i.e. every vertex of A meets w; then tau-transitivity gives all edges between A\B and B. Restricting to A: with A identified with Z_7 and sigma = +1, S = A\B and T = A n B are both nonempty proper subsets, and all S-T edges are present; applying sigma^k realizes every difference d != 0, because if S were closed under +d then S would be all of Z_7 (7 prime). Hence A becomes a clique; symmetrically B; so G[A u B] is complete on >= 8 vertices, giving at least 8! < extendable automorphisms. Contradiction. Sound.

Case 1 (A = B): <sigma,tau> fixes everything outside A and restricts faithfully to a subgroup of Sym(A) = S_7 generated by two 7-cycles, so it equals Aut(G) = PSL(2,7); then restriction to H = G[A] is an isomorphism Aut(G) -> Aut(H) (injective since elements fix the outside pointwise, surjective by the extension lemma), so H would be a 7-vertex graph with automorphism group PSL(2,7), excluded by the exhaustive check of the 1044 graphs on 7 vertices (and independently by 2-transitivity of PSL(3,2) on 7 points).

One misstatement, not fatal: line 0025 claims a subgroup of S_7 generated by two 7-cycles is C_7, PSL(2,7), or S_7. S_7 is actually impossible (7-cycles are even) and A_7 is missing: (1234567) and (1234576) are both 7-cycles whose quotient is the 3-cycle (1 7 6), and a primitive group of degree 7 containing a 3-cycle is A_7 by Jordan. However the omitted case A_7 has order 2520 > 168 and is killed by the proof's own stated reason ('too many automorphisms'), so the conclusion <sigma,tau> = PSL(2,7) still follows verbatim. This is a repairable slip in a classification aside, not a gap that breaks any step's conclusion, so the proof stands.
